defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: service.py:37 isinstance TextIO misses the os.devnull binary file opened by default, so it leaks
service.py:37 binary file objects passed as log_output fall through both branches and leak; use hasattr close
service.py:40 os.close may raise OSError now that the blanket except was removed
test_service.py:23 read_end not closed if stop() raises; use try/finally
service.py:18 pre-existing IO[Any] annotation mismatches the TextIO runtime check
votes.evidence_quote: `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` does not match the file created when `log_output=None`. Line 23 opens `open(os.devnull, "wb")`, which produces a `BufferedRandom` (binary mode). That object is neither `TextIO` nor `int`, so neither `close()` nor `os.close()` fires and the devnull file handle leaks.
votes.justification: The review flags the `isinstance(..., TextIO)` check in `stop()` as failing to match real file objects, so they stay open. It cites the default `os.devnull` log, and binary files generally, and proposes a general close-method check. It wrongly implies text-mode files do match, but it catches the core faulty check, its consequence and the fix at the right code.
